--- SOURCE 3: The Spatio-Temporal Distribution and Population Dynamics of Chub ... ---
URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12024016

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This study, published in Animals (an open-access MDPI journal) in April 2025, examines the spatio-temporal distribution and population dynamics of chub mackerel (Scomber japonicus) in the high seas of the Northwest Pacific Ocean (NPO). Authors: Guoqing Zhao, Heng Zhang, and Fenghua Tang (corresponding author: f-h-tang@163.com).

**Study Methodology:**
- Study area: High seas of the NPO between 35°N–45°N and 145°E–160°E
- Data: 38,123 fishing operations from Chinese commercial light purse seine vessel logs (2016–2021), plus 4,440 biological samples
- Methods: Length-weight relationships, Von Bertalanffy growth equations (ELEFAN I in FISAT II), mortality estimation (Pauly's equations), and Length-based Bayesian (LBB) stock assessment using the TropFishR package in R

**Key Findings:**
1. **Spatio-temporal distribution**: High catches were concentrated along the outer edge of Japan and Russia's EEZ lines. The gravity center of fishing grounds moved gradually northwestward from 2016-2021, with a northeast-southwest-northeast pattern. CPUE decreased year by year, with large values dominating 2016-2018 and small values dominating 2019-2021. Strong negative correlation existed between CPUE and year (r = -0.489, p < 0.01).

2. **Biological characteristics**: Sex ratios (female:male) ranged from 1.09 to 2.55 across years (all >1). Fork lengths ranged from 102 mm (2021) to 400 mm (2020). Mean lengths varied from 212.07 mm (2016) to 268.28 mm (2018). Growth parameters: asymptotic length (L inf) ranged 36-42.35 cm; growth coefficient K ranged 0.31-0.65.

3. **Stock assessment (LBB results)**: No overfishing occurred during 2016-2021. F/M ratios were all <0.5, E (exploitation rate) values ranged 0.17-0.32 (all below 0.5), B/B0 were all >0.5, B/Bmsy were all >1, L95th/Linf and Lmean/Lopt were close to 1, and Lc/Lopt were >1. All years were classified as "healthy" stock status with reasonable body length structure and presence of large individuals.

4. **Concerns**: Although not currently overexploited, the exploitation ratio (E) showed an increasing trend, reaching 0.48 by 2021 (from conventional methods), suggesting it may soon reach critical thresholds. The study emphasizes that climate warming, marine heatwaves (frequent in NPO since 2014), and increased competition with Japanese sardine are important factors affecting chub mackerel population dynamics.

**Explanations for CPUE decline despite healthy stock**: (1) Reasonable resource fluctuation not reaching critical population thresholds; (2) spawning grounds in south-central Pacific coast of Japan may have changed, reducing recruitment via Kuroshio Current transport; (3) increasing food competition with Japanese sardine, which also serves as a food source for adult chub mackerel; (4) interactions among proliferating fishing vessels' fish-attracting light systems.

**Conclusions**: (1) Fishing ground gravity center moved northward with year-by-year CPUE decline; (2) Chub mackerel grew well with no miniaturization and reasonable length structure; (3) Fishing mortality was low, no overfishing occurred; (4) E value increase warrants attention from international management organizations. Managers should consider climate warming impacts on marine ecosystem population composition.

Funding: National Key Research and Development Programme (2019YFD0901405) and Shanghai Frontiers Science Center of Polar Science Base Open Subject Fund (SOO2024-15).
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
## Chub Mackerel Tsushima Stock Assessment (2019)

### Stock Status Overview
The stock assessment of Chub Mackerel (Scomber japonicus) Tsushima stock was conducted by the National Research Institute of Fisheries Science and Saikai National Fisheries Research Institute. The stock biomass was around 1 million tons during 1973-1996, decreased to ~500,000 tons after 2000, then recovered to 650,000 tons in 2018 supported by strong recruitments. SSB in 2018 was estimated at ~238,000-240,000 tons.

### Key Reference Points
- **SBmsy**: 310,000 tons
- **Fmsy**: (0.33, 1.07, 0.69, 0.69) for ages 0, 1, 2, 3+ respectively

This webpage presents the abstract and article details for a scientific paper titled "Analysis of the inter-annual variation of chub mackerel abundance in the East China Sea and Yellow Sea during 1999-2011" published in the Journal of Fisheries of China (2014, 38(1): 56-64, DOI: 10.3724/SP.J.1231.2014.48737). The paper was authored by WANG Congjun, ZOU Lijin, LI Gang, and CHEN Xinjun.

The study analyzed chub mackerel (Scomber japonicus) catch data from the large lighting-purse seine fishery (1999-2011) using generalized linear models (GLM) and generalized additive models (GAM). Eight variables were examined: temporal factors (Year, Month), spatial factors (Longitude, Latitude), environmental factors (Sea surface temperature, Sea surface height, Sea surface chlorophyll-a concentration), and fishing performance (Vessel name) on catch per unit effort (CPUE).

Key findings include:
- The GAM with eight variables explains 11.69% of total variance in nominal CPUE, with "Year" being the foremost factor, contributing 53.9% of total reduction in deviance.
- Chub mackerel abundance showed a declining trend over the 13-year period, especially after 2008, with the abundance index (AI) falling from 1.22 in 2008 to 0.82 in 2011.
- The AI showed a significantly positive relationship with sea surface temperature (SST) of the spawning ground, expressed as AI = -3.5 + 0.23SST (P < 0.05).
- The decline in chub mackerel abundance is attributed to the rapidly increasing number of purse seine vessels in recent years, suggesting overfishing pressure as a primary driver of population decline.
</summary>

"The GAM with the eight variables explains 11.69% of the total variance in nominal CPUE, and the impact of Year on CPUE is the foremost factor, contributing to 53.9% of the total reduction in deviance."

--- SOURCE 15: Review of population dynamics and management of small pelagic fishes around the Japanese Archipelago ---
URL: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12562-019-01305-3

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an open-access peer-reviewed review article published in Fisheries Science (Springer/journal 12562) on April 3, 2019, by Akihiko Yatsu (Volume 85, pages 611-639). The article reviews the population dynamics and management of small pelagic fishes (SPF) around the Japanese Archipelago, focusing on four target species: Japanese sardine (Sardinops melanostictus), Japanese anchovy (Engraulis japonicus), chub mackerel (Scomber japonicus), and Pacific saury (Cololabis saira). The article has 20k accesses and 113 citations.

Key findings:
- SPF catch and biomass show decadal-scale variability with prominent species replacements since the 1900s, driven largely by climatic/oceanic variability and "regime shifts." The 1988/89 regime shift was the most influential since the 1970s.
- Variability in early survival rate is a key factor for population fluctuations.
- Overfishing during the 1990s and early 2000s prevented recovery of Pacific stocks of sardine and chub mackerel, but both have been recovering since the mid-2000s due to strong year classes and reduced exploitation rates.
- The fundamental cause of overfishing stemmed from a mismatch between investments in larger purse seine fleets during the 1980s and poor ocean productivity following the 1988/89 regime shift, when dominant SPF shifted from sardine to anchovy.

Population dynamics context:
- Paleoecological evidence (scale deposition rates from Beppu Bay, Japan) covering 2,850 years shows sardine periodicities of approximately 50, 100, and 300 years, while anchovy shows periodicities of approximately 30 and 260 years—indicating decadal-scale alternations in the 20th century did not necessarily occur in earlier periods.
- During the 20th century, Pacific sardines flourished during warmer global air temperatures and positive PDO phases, while anchovies flourished during negative PDO phases.

Oceanographic setting:
- The Northwestern Pacific (FAO Statistical Area 61) is the most productive area worldwide, involving interactions of the Tsushima, Kuroshio, Kuroshio Extension, and Oyashio Currents, plus marginal seas (East China Sea, Yellow Sea, Japan Sea, Seto Inland Sea, Sea of Okhotsk).
- Annual average sea surface temperature around Japan has increased +1.11°C over the last 100 years, exceeding the global ocean (+0.54°C) and North Pacific (+0.51°C) averages.

Management considerations:
- Six climatic/oceanic indices affect target stock dynamics: North Pacific Index (NPI), Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO), Kuroshio Extension South Area SST (KESA), North Pacific Gyre Oscillation (NPGO), Arctic Oscillation (AO), and Monsoon Index (MOI).
- Management challenges arise because recruitment and surplus production are strongly affected by environmental variability, including regime shifts.
- Pacific saury is managed internationally under the North Pacific Fisheries Commission (NPFC), established 2015.
- The article provides recommendations for SPF fisheries management around Japan considering climate change and naturally fluctuating SPF populations.
</summary>

"Population dynamics of small pelagic fishes (SPF) and their management in Japan were reviewed for Japanese sardine Sardinops melanostictus, Japanese anchovy Engraulis japonicus, chub mackerel Scomber japonicus, and Pacific saury Cololabis saira."

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from the Global Seafood Alliance's Responsible Seafood Advocate, authored by Sukgeun Jung, Ph.D. (Jeju National University, Republic of Korea), summarizes a study published in Fishes (2025, 10(1), 20) by Go, S. et al. that projects how climate change will shift the spawning grounds of chub mackerel (Scomber japonicus) in the Western North Pacific Ocean.

**Key background:** Chub mackerel are forage fish crucial to marine food webs, feeding on zooplankton/phytoplankton and serving as prey for larger marine predators. The Tsushima Warm Current (TWC) stock is an economically valuable fishery exploited by China, Korea, and Japan, spawning mainly in the East China Sea (ECS) and Korea Strait (KS) from February to June before migrating to northern feeding grounds in the Japan/East Sea (JES) and Yellow Sea (YS).

**Study methodology:** Researchers developed spawning ground indices and used the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) to estimate and project water temperature and salinity at 10 meters depth in the western North Pacific. The model simulated ocean conditions from 2010 to 2059 under an IPCC Fifth Assessment Report (IPCC AR5) climate change scenario, comparing the 2010s (2010–2019) and 2050s (2050–2059) periods.

**Key findings:**
- Potential spawning grounds were projected to shift northward from the 2010s to the 2050s, meaning chub mackerel will spawn further north in the 2050s and become less influenced by the Kuroshio Current.
- This northward shift is expected to cause a subsequent westward shift of nursery grounds (from the Pacific side of Japan and JES toward waters off Jeju Island), consistent with earlier work by Li et al.
- Ratios of exploitable chub mackerel biomass and production are expected to increase in the Korea Strait and Yellow Sea relative to the JES.
- Model outputs were generally compatible with previous observations, though the model did not perfectly align with observational data in the same space and time; data assimilation methods were suggested for future improvements.
- Spawning grounds were assumed to be limited to continental shelf areas (50–300 meters depth), though other research suggests chub mackerel may also spawn in shallower coastal areas (<50 meters), including Kagoshima Bay and Osumi Strait.
- The study only considered environmental conditions at 10 meters depth and used only temperature and salinity variables; other factors (turbulence, currents, dissolved oxygen) and photoperiod influences on spawning periods require further research.

**Conclusions:** The study enhances the reliability of stock assessment for fisheries management of chub mackerel and contributes to the development of individual-based bio-physical coupled models for predicting recruitment and spatiotemporal distribution of exploitable chub mackerel. The results are expected to inform fisheries policies accounting for climate change in the region.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Potential spawning grounds were projected to shift northward from the 2010s to 2050s, and these suggested that chub mackerel will spawn further north in the 2050s compared to the 2010s, which means that spawning will become less strongly influenced by the Kuroshio Current."
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 1: and inter-specific density dependence of body condition ... ---
URL: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.03.25.436928.full

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a bioRxiv preprint (DOI: 10.1101/2021.03.25.436928) titled "Intra- and inter-specific density dependence of body condition, growth, and habitat temperature in chub mackerel (Scomber japonicus)" by Yasuhiro Kamimura, Makoto Taga, Ryuji Yukami, Chikako Watanabe, and Sho Furuichi (Japan Fisheries Research and Education Agency). It has since been published in ICES Journal of Marine Science (doi: 10.1093/icesjms/fsab191).

**Research Question & Hypothesis:** The study investigated how conspecific (chub mackerel) and heterospecific (Japanese sardine, Sardinops melanostictus) abundance affects body condition, growth, and habitat temperature in chub mackerel in the western North Pacific. The authors hypothesized that body condition is affected both directly (competition for food) and indirectly (through changes in habitat temperature) by population density.

**Key Findings:**
- Chub mackerel body condition, habitat temperature, and growth all decreased with increasing conspecific and heterospecific abundance.
- Mean annual growth rates were positively correlated with body condition in all four quarters (Q1: χ²=34.6, p<0.001; Q2: χ²=7.23, p=0.007; Q3: χ²=6.50, p=0.011; Q4: χ²=4.83, p=0.028).
- The best structural equation model (SEM) showed that conspecific and/or heterospecific abundance had strong negative effects on body condition in all seasons, and influenced habitat temperature in some seasons, but temperature effects on body condition were weak.
- Direct effects (food competition) likely have more impact than indirect effects (habitat temperature changes) on density-dependent body condition and growth.

**Methodology:**
- 18,302 chub mackerel landed in fishing ports on the Pacific coast of northern Japan (2006–2019) were sampled; 68% from purse seine fisheries.
- 15,415 fish from 2006–2016 year classes used for growth analysis with von Bertalanffy growth equations.
- 8,429 age-1+ fish used for relative condition factor (Kn) analysis.
- Habitat temperature estimated using FRA-ROMS ocean model reanalysis data.
- Piecewise structural equation models (SEMs) with linear mixed models used for statistical analysis, applied quarterly (Q1 spawning, Q2 northward feeding migration, Q3 southward migration, Q4 pre-spawning).
- Age-1+ chub mackerel abundance ranged from 8.5×10⁹ (2007) to 141.2×10⁹ individuals (2017); Japanese sardine abundance ranged from 5.2×10⁹ (2008) to 313.6×10⁹ individuals (2018).
- Weight-length relationship: W = 1.09 × 10⁻⁶ L³.⁴¹.
- VB parameter estimates: Linf ranged 339.9–440.5, K ranged 0.25–0.55, t0 ranged −2.88 to −1.26.

**Context:**
Chub mackerel is a globally important fishery resource with annual catches around 1.5 million metric tons. The Pacific stock declined in the 1990s–early 2000s but dramatically increased after a strong 2013 year class. Japanese sardine, a potential competitor with overlapping prey (Copepoda, Eupausiidae, Decapoda, Amphipoda) and distributions, has also increased over the past decade. This study addresses gaps in understanding density-dependent processes during periods of population increase.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"The density dependence of growth and body condition have important impacts on fish population dynamics and fisheries management." — Abstract
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 3: The Spatio-Temporal Distribution and Population Dynamics of Chub ... ---
URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12024016

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This study, published in Animals (an open-access MDPI journal) in April 2025, examines the spatio-temporal distribution and population dynamics of chub mackerel (Scomber japonicus) in the high seas of the Northwest Pacific Ocean (NPO). Authors: Guoqing Zhao, Heng Zhang, and Fenghua Tang (corresponding author: f-h-tang@163.com).

**Study Methodology:**
- Study area: High seas of the NPO between 35°N–45°N and 145°E–160°E
- Data: 38,123 fishing operations from Chinese commercial light purse seine vessel logs (2016–2021), plus 4,440 biological samples
- Methods: Length-weight relationships, Von Bertalanffy growth equations (ELEFAN I in FISAT II), mortality estimation (Pauly's equations), and Length-based Bayesian (LBB) stock assessment using the TropFishR package in R

**Key Findings:**
1. **Spatio-temporal distribution**: High catches were concentrated along the outer edge of Japan and Russia's EEZ lines. The gravity center of fishing grounds moved gradually northwestward from 2016-2021, with a northeast-southwest-northeast pattern. CPUE decreased year by year, with large values dominating 2016-2018 and small values dominating 2019-2021. Strong negative correlation existed between CPUE and year (r = -0.489, p < 0.01).

2. **Biological characteristics**: Sex ratios (female:male) ranged from 1.09 to 2.55 across years (all >1). Fork lengths ranged from 102 mm (2021) to 400 mm (2020). Mean lengths varied from 212.07 mm (2016) to 268.28 mm (2018). Growth parameters: asymptotic length (L inf) ranged 36-42.35 cm; growth coefficient K ranged 0.31-0.65.

3. **Stock assessment (LBB results)**: No overfishing occurred during 2016-2021. F/M ratios were all <0.5, E (exploitation rate) values ranged 0.17-0.32 (all below 0.5), B/B0 were all >0.5, B/Bmsy were all >1, L95th/Linf and Lmean/Lopt were close to 1, and Lc/Lopt were >1. All years were classified as "healthy" stock status with reasonable body length structure and presence of large individuals.

4. **Concerns**: Although not currently overexploited, the exploitation ratio (E) showed an increasing trend, reaching 0.48 by 2021 (from conventional methods), suggesting it may soon reach critical thresholds. The study emphasizes that climate warming, marine heatwaves (frequent in NPO since 2014), and increased competition with Japanese sardine are important factors affecting chub mackerel population dynamics.

**Explanations for CPUE decline despite healthy stock**: (1) Reasonable resource fluctuation not reaching critical population thresholds; (2) spawning grounds in south-central Pacific coast of Japan may have changed, reducing recruitment via Kuroshio Current transport; (3) increasing food competition with Japanese sardine, which also serves as a food source for adult chub mackerel; (4) interactions among proliferating fishing vessels' fish-attracting light systems.

**Conclusions**: (1) Fishing ground gravity center moved northward with year-by-year CPUE decline; (2) Chub mackerel grew well with no miniaturization and reasonable length structure; (3) Fishing mortality was low, no overfishing occurred; (4) E value increase warrants attention from international management organizations. Managers should consider climate warming impacts on marine ecosystem population composition.

Funding: National Key Research and Development Programme (2019YFD0901405) and Shanghai Frontiers Science Center of Polar Science Base Open Subject Fund (SOO2024-15).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"From 2016 to 2021, high catches of chub mackerel were concentrated along the outer edge of Japan or Russia's exclusive economic zone line, and the gravity center of the fishing grounds moved to the northwest gradually, with a decrease in the average value of catch per unit effort (CPUE) year by year."
</key_excerpts>

URL: https://www.mdpi.com/2077-1312/10/2/301

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a peer-reviewed open-access scientific article published in the Journal of Marine Science and Engineering (JMSE) in 2022. The article, "Growth Heterogeneity of Chub Mackerel (Scomber japonicus) in the Northwest Pacific Ocean," was authored by Kai Cai, Richard Kindong, Qiuyun Ma (corresponding author), Xiaobin Han, and Song Qin from Shanghai Ocean University and the Zhejiang Mariculture Research Institute, China. The DOI is 10.3390/jmse10020301, published on 21 February 2022, and belongs to the special issue "Marine Fish and Invertebrate Aquaculture."

**Study Overview:** The research evaluated the growth heterogeneity and ageing analysis of Chub mackerel, a commercially exploited pelagic fish widely distributed in temperate and subtropical zones of the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Data were collected from Chinese fishing vessels from 2016–2020 in the northwest Pacific Ocean, covering two regions: the Zhejiang coastal area and the high seas near Japan.

**Key Findings:**
- 2,686 specimens were analyzed with fork lengths ranging from 40–294 mm (average 181.91 mm) and body weights from 0.8–311.8 g (average 73.27 g). The dominant fork length group was 210–220 mm, and dominant weight group was 20–30 g.
- The length-weight relationship was determined as W = (1.41 × 10⁻⁶) × FL³·³⁷.
- Seven linear mixed-effects models (LMEM) were used to analyze heterogeneity. The best-fitting model included random effects for year, season, and region on the scaling parameter "a." Differences in parameter "a" were larger for years (7.66 × 10⁻⁷) than regions (5.57 × 10⁻⁷) or seasons (3.20 × 10⁻⁷).
- Growth heterogeneity was most pronounced for specimens larger than 200 mm fork length, with significant variation by year and region. Summer showed significantly lower growth rates for larger fish.
- Age estimation was performed on 175 specimens using otoliths. Ages ranged from 0–5 years (13 age-0, 54 age-1, 60 age-2, 40 age-3, 7 age-4, 1 age-5 otoliths). The age-bias plot showed no systematic bias between two independent readers.
- Three non-linear growth models were tested (von Bertalanffy, logistic, and Gompertz). The von Bertalanffy growth model (VBGF) provided the best fit based on AIC and BIC values. Individual Chub mackerel exhibited a slower growth rate than observed in previous studies.
- For Zhejiang coastal samples (which lacked sufficient otoliths), ELEFAN I analysis in FiSAT II software was used to fit growth parameters.
- Relative condition factors varied among years, seasons, and regions. Only K relative to 2006–16 and 2016 reference periods had mean values higher than 1. The lowest relative condition factor was observed in 2017, and summer had the highest seasonal condition factors. Fork length was significantly greater in 2020 than other years, and the median fork length in the high seas near Japan (220 mm) was much higher than in the Zhejiang coastal area (150 mm).

**Methodological Details:** Samples were collected via bottom trawling in Zhejiang coastal waters (four seasonal surveys annually, 2016–2020) using an 800 t gross registered ton vessel with 403 kW engine power, and from high seas near Japan (June, July, September 2020) aboard the vessel "Fu yuan yu 601." Otoliths were prepared using resin embedding, polishing with graded sandpaper (150–2000 grit), and examined under an Olympus microscope (SZX 23) at 100× magnification. Model fitting and statistical analyses were performed in R (Version 4.0.3) using packages including lme4, Matrix, nlme, Metrics, rjstat, and FSA.

**Conclusion:** The study provides an effective scientific basis for stock assessment and fishery management of Chub mackerel in the northwest Pacific Ocean, highlighting significant spatiotemporal growth heterogeneity driven largely by year-to-year variation.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 6: [PDF] Fish debris in sediments from the last 25 kyr in the Humboldt Current ... ---
URL: https://archimer.ifremer.fr/doc/00500/61147/64575.pdf

SUMMARY:
<summary>
## Scientific Paper Summary: Fish Debris in Sediments from the Last 25 kyr in the Humboldt Current

### Study Overview
This peer-reviewed paper (Salvatteci et al., 2019, *Progress in Oceanography*, Vol. 176, doi:10.1016/j.pocean.2019.05.006) reconstructs past changes in small pelagic fish populations in the Humboldt Current System (HCS) off Peru over the last 25,000 years, examining their response to changes in oxygen minimum zone (OMZ) intensity and marine productivity.

### Key Findings
- **Productivity is the main factor controlling small pelagic fish abundance**, while sub-surface oxygenation affects anchovy and likely sardine populations in species-dependent ways.
- **Lower productivity and higher oxygen during the glacial period** resulted in lower total fish productivity; **higher productivity and stronger OMZ during the Holocene** resulted in higher fish abundances.
- **Anchovy (Engraulis ringens) were the predominant small pelagic fish throughout the entire 25-kyr record**, comprising ~90% of all fish scales identified.
- **No evidence of out-of-phase relationships between anchovy and sardine** at the timescales examined (centennial to millennial).
- **Anchovy abundance reached a maximum during the Current Warm Period (CWP)**, characterized by high productivity and intense OMZ conditions—meaning the industrial fishery developed during a period of exceptional productivity relative to the last 25 kyr.
- **Dramatic decreases in pelagic fish abundances have occurred in response to past large-scale climate changes** larger than those observed in the instrumental period, suggesting future climate change may cause substantial ecosystem restructuring.

### Methodology
- Fish scales and bones from laminated sediments off Pisco (~14°S), central-southern Peru were quantified and identified at an average sampling resolution of 20.4 years (±7.1).
- Three sediment cores were used: box core B05-14 (1518–2004 AD), gravity core G-10 (0.45–10.3 kyr BP), and gravity core G-14 (13.4–25.2 kyr BP).
- Nearly 120,000 pieces of fish debris were classified and counted.
- Species identified to species level: anchovy, sardine, jack mackerel, chub mackerel, hake, and saury; mesopelagic fishes quantified as a group.
- Preservation indices (integrity index, bio-degradation index, scale-to-vertebrae ratio) were developed and compared with environmental proxies (Mo/Re ratios, δ15N for oxygenation; TOC, Ni Enrichment Factor, CaCO3 for export production).
- Statistical analyses included Spearman correlations, Kruskal-Wallis tests, Generalized Additive Models (GAMs), and Principal Component Analysis.

### Key Species Context
- **Anchovy (E. ringens)**: r-type species, short lifespan (~4 years), inhabits water above the oxycline in cold coastal upwelled water.
- **Sardine (Sardinops sagax)**: larger than anchovy, does not tolerate low oxygen, distributed further offshore at the border of intense upwelling zones.
- **Jack mackerel**: long-lived (16 years), wide distribution across the South Pacific; distribution associated with sub-surface oxygen.
- **Hake (Merluccius gayi peruanus)**: demersal species that tolerates hypoxia (oxygen 0.13–2.77 ml/l).
- **Mesopelagic fishes**: dominate the Peruvian mesopelagic community (e.g., Vinciguerria lucetia with an estimated 14 million tonnes biomass in 2003), many adapted to live in oxygen-deficient waters.

### Study Context
The HCS off Peru represents 0.1% of the world ocean but can produce up to 10% of the world fish catch. The study spans the Last Glacial Maximum (23–19 kyr BP), Termination 1 (19–11.4 kyr BP, including Heinrich 1 Stadial and Antarctic Cold Reversal), and the Holocene (11.5 kyr BP to present). The future of Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems under climate change is uncertain, with models predicting either increased stratification or upwelling, and potential reductions in plankton due to nutrient depletion.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Our results reveal that productivity appears to be the main factor controlling small pelagic fish abundance, while sub-surface oxygenation affects mainly anchovy and likely sardine populations."
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 7: A summary report of life history information on Pacific ... ---
URL: https://repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/52097/noaa_52097_DS1.pdf

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This NOAA Technical Memorandum (NMFS-SWFSC-689, August 2023) provides a detailed summary of life history information collected and analyzed for Pacific mackerel (Scomber japonicus) used in the 2023 benchmark stock assessment. The report was authored by researchers from NOAA Fisheries' Southwest Fisheries Science Center (SWFSC), Lynker Technologies, UC Santa Cruz's Cooperative Institute for Marine, Earth, and Atmospheric Systems (CIMEAS), and the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW).

**Purpose and Data Sources:** The report aims to: (1) provide updated age and length data; (2) compute ageing error matrices for the stock assessment model; (3) provide updated estimates of length and age at maturity; and (4) discuss future life history research priorities. Biological samples were collected from spring 2010-2021 and summer 2012-2022 SWFSC trawl surveys (otoliths and ovaries) and from monthly CDFW Port Sampling Program fishery samples from 2008-2022 (otoliths only). Ages were assigned using a July 1 birthdate convention, and ovaries were histologically processed for maturity classification.

**Key Results—Age and Length Data:**
- SWFSC survey fish (2012-2022, n=1,762 aged) ranged from 53-402 mm FL and ages 0-7 years. Age composition was dominated by young fish: age 0 (46%), 1 (29%), 2 (16%), 3 (6%), with ages 4-7 comprising only 2.3% of samples.
- CDFW port sampling (2008-2022, n=9,035 aged) ranged from 84-429 mm FL and ages 0-9 years, with ages 0-3 representing 47%, 30%, 12%, and 7% respectively; ages 4-9 comprised only 4%.
- All-read samples from 2008-2017 (n=1,614 otoliths) showed high agreement for ages 0-1 (94% and 78%), moderate for ages 2-3 (52% and 41%), and low for ages 4-6 (22-30%). Survey data (n=643) showed 100% agreement for ages 0-2, 94% at age 3, 75% at age 4, and 70% at age 5.

**Key Results—Maturity:**
- A total of 911 female gonad samples (174-402 mm FL, ages 0-7) were histologically examined using standardized terminology (Brown-Peterson et al. 2011). Age data were available for 494 females.
- Length at maturity (L50) was estimated at 274 ± 1.26 mm FL, with all females (L95) at 309 ± 2.60 mm FL predicted mature.
- Age at maturity (A50) was 1.01 ± 0.06 years, with all females older than 2.52 ± 0.15 years predicted mature. The L50 is nearly identical to previous estimates, but A50 is lower than the previous estimate of 2.2 years, attributed to improved ageing precision and greater availability of small age classes in surveys. Results indicate maturity schedules have remained constant over recent decades.

**Future Research Priorities:** (1) Collect data from Mexican waters (where a significant proportion of commercial catch occurs) through collaboration or surveys to cover the full population range; (2) improve age estimation by coordinating between ageing labs, standardizing age reads, refining age-reading error quantification, and developing a fecundity-weight relationship.

**Context:** Pacific mackerel is one of five coastal pelagic species under the PFMC's CPS Fishery Management Plan. The 2023 benchmark assessment estimated total biomass of 93,823 metric tons for 2021 (86.9% from ages 0-2), with projected spawning stock biomass of 46,167 mt (2023) and 50,372 mt (2024). The species is managed as a single unit by the PFMC under a quota system, with the fishery reopening in 1977 after a moratorium following a mid-1960s population decline.

--- SOURCE 8: Development of characterization factors for Peruvian fish ... ---
URL: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11367-026-02626-z

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article, published in The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment (Volume 31, article 69, 2026) as open access, presents the development of characterization factors (CFs) for 10 Peruvian fishing stocks within the Fisheries Impact Pathway (FIP) framework for Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The authors (Rubén Manrique-Muñante, Alejandro Deville, Ramzy Kahhat, and Ian Vázquez-Rowe, all from the same institution) address the gap that biodiversity impacts of Peruvian fisheries—strongly influenced by El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)—are not fully covered by current LCIA models.

Key methodological aspects include: (1) optimization of CMSY++ stock assessment model performance using exhaustive statistical analysis (including retrospective, hindcasting, biological plausibility, and jittering analyses); (2) calculation of CF time series (2007–2023) under an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) approach for anchoveta, jack mackerel, chub mackerel, bonito, hake, common dolphinfish, skipjack tuna, jumbo squid and calico scallop; (3) statistical evaluation of enhanced CFs including uncertainty, sensitivity analyses, and correlation with ENSO indices; and (4) application of CFs in case studies for direct and indirect human consumption fisheries.

Key findings:
- Enhanced CFs deviate up to 4 orders of magnitude from previously reported values, usually showing lower values
- CFs exhibit weak-moderate statistical correlation with typical ENSO indices, with sea level anomalies showing the strongest relationship
- Case studies in the Peruvian EEZ confirmed significant differences in fishing impacts for stocks destined to direct human consumption during El Niño and La Niña years, with additional LCIA impacts ranging from 0.1% to 61% in fishmeal and fish oil production among plants of a major producer during 2019 and 2021

Background context: Peru is one of the most important fishing nations globally, with Peruvian anchoveta (Engraulis ringens) being the largest fishery worldwide by volume. Approximately 95% of landed anchoveta goes to fishmeal and fish oil (FMFO) production, supplying 15–20% of global FMFO. Other species (jack mackerel, bonito, chub mackerel, hake, jumbo squid, calico scallop) contribute to about 20% of annual landings and generated 2600 million US$ in export revenue in 2023. The historical context includes the fishery collapse in 1972 driven by ENSO and overfishing, after which quota systems (individual quotas for industrial fleet since 2009, artisanal fleet TAC since 2017) have helped maintain stock health.

The authors argue that the enhanced CF time series more accurately represents stock population dynamics under fluctuating climatic stressors and management regimes than the original FIP method, responding to international LCA guidelines calling for regionalized and temporally explicit impact assessment. The study recommends using these CFs for assessing biotic resource depletion in Peruvian seafood and aquaculture systems, and extending the methodology to other EEZs affected by similar ecosystem dynamics and fishing pressure.
</summary>

"Enhanced CFs deviate up to 4 orders of magnitude from previously reported values, usually showing lower values. These CFs also exhibit weak-moderate statistical correlation with typical ENSO indices, with sea level anomalies showing the strongest relationship."

SUMMARY:
<summary>
## Chub Mackerel Tsushima Stock Assessment (2019)

### Stock Status Overview
The stock assessment of Chub Mackerel (Scomber japonicus) Tsushima stock was conducted by the National Research Institute of Fisheries Science and Saikai National Fisheries Research Institute. The stock biomass was around 1 million tons during 1973-1996, decreased to ~500,000 tons after 2000, then recovered to 650,000 tons in 2018 supported by strong recruitments. SSB in 2018 was estimated at ~238,000-240,000 tons.

### Key Reference Points
- **SBmsy**: 310,000 tons
- **Fmsy**: (0.33, 1.07, 0.69, 0.69) for ages 0, 1, 2, 3+ respectively
- **%SPR(Fmsy)**: 20%
- **MSY**: 323,000 tons
- **SB2018/SBmsy**: 0.77 (below SBmsy)
- **F2018/Fmsy**: 1.24 (above Fmsy)
- Stock-recruitment relationship: Hockey Stick (HS) model, no autocorrelation (parameters: a=0.00755, b=237,192 tons)

### Stock Status Summary (2018)
- SSB: Below SBmsy (warning level)
- Fishing pressure (F): Above Fmsy
- SSB trend (2014-2018): Increasing

### Biology and Ecology
- **Distribution**: Southern East China Sea to northern Japan Sea, Yellow Sea, and Bo Hai
- **Growth**: 25-28cm FL at age 1, 29-32cm at age 2, 33-35cm at age 3, 36cm at age 4, 37cm at age 5; longevity ~6 years
- **Spawning**: Main grounds in East China Sea off Chinese coast, Korean Peninsula coastal waters, and Kyusyu/Sanin coastal waters of Japan; season Jan-Apr in south, May-Jun in north
- **Maturity**: 60% at age 1, 85% at age 2, 100% at age 3+
- **Natural mortality (M)**: 0.4 per year

### Fisheries and Catches
- Mainly caught by purse seine fisheries in East China Sea, Korean coastal waters, northwest Kyusyu, and western Japan Sea
- Japanese catch 2018: 150,000 tons (0- and 1-year old fish dominate); Korean catch 2018: 140,000 tons (age composition unknown); Chinese catch up to 500,000 tons since 2010 (species composition unknown, NOT included in analysis)
- Total catch 2018 (Japan + Korea): 292,000 tons
- Fishing effort (purse seine nets) at lowest level (4,710 nets) in 2018 due to shift to Pacific fishing grounds

### Assessment Methodology
- Cohort analysis (VPA) using catch-at-age data from Japan and Korea, tuned with abundance indices from purse seine fisheries
- Abundance indices from purse seine logbooks, Sakai port landing data, neuston-net larval surveys, acoustic surveys, and bottom trawl surveys
- Chinese catch excluded due to unreliable species composition data
- Results used as qualitative information due to insufficient accuracy of survey estimates

### Historical Trends
- **Biomass**: 1,000,000 tons (1973-1989), peaked 1,370,000 tons (1996), fell to 370,000 tons (2013, lowest), recovered to 654,000 tons (2018)
- **SSB**: Peaked 470,000 tons (1993-1996), dropped to 120,000 tons (2003), fluctuated 110,000-190,000 until 2014, increased to 240,000 tons (2018)
- **Recruitment**: Peak 3,300 million (1995), dropped to 800 million (2013), strong year classes 1,500 million (2014) and 2,000 million (2017), 1,329 million (2018)
- **Fishing ratio (U)**: Rapidly increased 1996, stayed high at 40-50%, was 45% in 2018
- **%SPR**: Lowest in 1996 (8.31%), was 16.7% in 2018 and 15.6% for F2016-2018 (below Fmsy level of 20%)

### Management Context
- Management via effort control (licensed vessels for purse seine) and TAC for "mackerels" (including blue mackerel) since 1997
- Stock rebuilding plan for western Japan Sea/western Kyusyu (2009-2011) focused on protecting juveniles
- Major uncertainty from lack of Chinese catch data; satellite night vision monitoring of Chinese fishing vessels started 2014
- Future projections complicated by inaccurate Chinese/Korean predictions and TAC combining chub and blue mackerel
- Recommended international cooperation for fisheries monitoring and further study of recruitment fluctuation and migration patterns
</summary>

Crucially, the BSS model incorporated a 2% annual technical creep correction to CPUE data—a factor frequently overlooked in previous research. The analysis used 55 years of catch data (1970–2024) from Korea, China, and Japan (Tsushima Current stock), plus 27 years of CPUE data (1997–2023) from Korea. - BSS estimated: r=0.310, k=1,802,382 tons, MSY=139,902 tons, B2024=549,884 tons.
- Kobe plot analysis revealed sustained high fishing mortality since the early 2000s has impeded recovery, with 87.6% (CMSY++) and 95.3% (BSS) posterior probability of the stock remaining in the "overfished and overfishing" red quadrant.

**Conclusions:** The study demonstrates CMSY++ as an effective tool for reconciling discrepancies in data-limited stock assessments and underscores the necessity of correcting for technical creep. Landing data from the Busan Cooperative Fish Market shows an increasing proportion of small-sized (≤250g, ~29.7cm TL, below the L50 of 31.4cm) immature individuals in the catch (from 65% in 2015 to 88% in 2024), providing biological evidence of stock depletion. </summary>

**Catches:** Landings from 2008-2022 were included from Mexico (Ensenada and Magdalena Bay) and the U.S. (California commercial and recreational, Oregon, Washington, plus bycatch from the Pacific whiting at-sea fishery). **Harvest Control Rule:** The MSY control rule is: Harvest = (Biomass − Cutoff) × E_MSY × Distribution, where Cutoff = 18,200 mt, E_MSY = 30%, and Distribution = 70%. Harvest guidelines have remained roughly 20,000-25,000 mt since 2015. The U.S. fishery has not fully utilized HGs since the late 1990s, with landings typically 7-39% of the HG (e.g., 990 mt USA landings in 2022 vs. 4,822 mt HG). Mexico's fishery is not regulated by quotas but has had minimum size limits (e.g., 25.5 cm); no international management agreements exist between the U.S. and Mexico for this transboundary stock.

**Ecosystem and History:** Pacific mackerel are part of the CPS (coastal pelagic species) assemblage in the California Current Ecosystem, though typically less abundant than anchovy or sardine. The stock experiences cyclical abundance periods (high biomass events roughly every 60 years). California first implemented management in 1970 with a moratorium. The federal FMP was implemented in January 2000 by the PFMC.

args.summary:
This is a YouTube video transcript from the channel "暴走麥克Traveler Mac" (Traveler Mac), posted on February 9, 2026, with approximately 23,271 views and 628 likes. The video explores the 大世界水產批發中心 (Dàshìjiè Seafood Wholesale Center) in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, China, which is located near the Zhoushan Islands fishing grounds—the largest fishing grounds in China.

The creator documents two visits to the wholesale market. On the first daytime visit, he discovers that fresh fish caught by fishing boats are only sold in the evening, not during the day. A stall owner explains that the wholesale center sells dried goods and processed products during the day, while live/fresh seafood (both farmed and wild-caught) arrives around 4-6 PM daily. The market is divided into sections: dried goods, live aquatic tanks (farmed seafood), and fresh catches from fishing boats sold on the ground after 4 PM.

Key price information gathered during the video:
- 白帶魚 (White belt fish/haittail): 16 yuan per jin (approximately 80 NTD)
- 黃花魚 (Yellow croaker): Prices range from 260 to 400 yuan per jin depending on size (wild-caught more expensive, one large one at 400 yuan/jin equals over 2,000 NTD)
- 墨魚 (Cuttlefish): 15-16 yuan per jin
- 海鰻 (Sea eel): 20 yuan per jin; one massive eel weighed over 30 jin
- 鱸魚 (Wild sea bass): 20 yuan per jin, with large ones over 100 yuan
- 陽澄湖大閘蟹 (Yangcheng Lake hairy crabs): About 55 yuan each for 4-5 liang (ounces) sized crabs; 5 liang is the largest size available; sold year-round, not just during Mid-Autumn Festival
- 魚卵 (Fish roe): 4 yuan per jin

The market operates from approximately 5-6 PM to 9 PM for fresh boat catches, with buyers including hotel and restaurant buyers and market vendors. The market does not offer processing/cooking services, so the creator visits 木暮海鮮 (Mùmù Seafood), a famous Ningbo restaurant, to try the city's renowned 黃魚麵 (yellow croaker noodle soup), which costs approximately 56 yuan per bowl and includes yellow croaker, shrimp, clams, and egg dumplings in a rich, milky broth.

This webpage is from the Zhoushan (舟山) Aquatic Products Association website (zsea.cn) in China. The content is a forecast/news article published on July 18, 2025, titled "Squid prices expected to rise 20-30%, industry must prepare for supply challenges."

Key points from the article:
- Experts at an industry forum predict that squid prices will rise by 20-30% in the 2025-2026 period, recovering from the historic low levels recorded in 2024 (which hit a record low cost of 11.4 yuan per kilogram, approximately 1 yuan per 10 jin... a significant low point).
- The global supply of squid is currently under pressure, particularly due to declining fisheries catches. In 2025, the catch is expected to drop by 22% to 57.7 thousand tons, with a possibility of further decline in 2026.
- The reduced supply is attributed to overfishing in the South Atlantic squid fisheries and other factors.
- Korea's squid processing industry has seen production facilities grow, with frozen squid fillet products representing 55% of processed squid products, and food products accounting for 10%. China's market for these products has grown 35% between 2020-2024, reaching 1.2 thousand tons (or 10 thousand tons), with products from Japan, Korea, and others being the main sources.
- The "low" price environment (30-35% of past price levels) for squid products is forcing companies to adapt.
- Industry experts indicate that under the dual pressures of reduced supply and increased demand, squid prices will gradually rise and stabilize, while producers face sustained cost pressures.

<webpage_content>
# [朝日新聞](https://www.asahi.com/?iref=pc_gnavi)

# サバ缶ブーム失速、ツナ缶に抜かれ5年で半減　「需要はあるのに」

[有料記事](//www.asahi.com/news/gold.html?iref=com_gold)

![写真・図版]()

　手頃な価格と健康志向でブームを巻き起こしたサバ缶が、勢いを失っている。生産量は5年で半減。背景には、深刻なサバ不足がある。

　「サバ缶の生産量は、10年前の30分の1にまで落ち込んでいます」

[宮城県](https://www.asahi.com/area/miyagi/ "宮城県 のトピックスを開く")[石巻市](//www.asahi.com/topics/word/石巻市.html "石巻市 のトピックスを開く")の水産加工会社「木の屋石巻水産」の松友倫人営業部課長は苦しい胸の内を明かす。

　東北有数の水揚げ量を誇る石巻港の「金華サバ」を使った水煮やみそ煮の缶詰を作ってきた。だが、ここ数年は水揚げ量が振るわず、サイズも小ぶりに。缶詰の原料がそろわず、休売を繰り返している。「この3年で、缶詰用のサバの仕入れ価格は2倍に跳ね上がりました。先行きが見通せません」

## 震災復興の「サヴァ缶」も終了

[東日本大震災](http://www.asahi.com/shinsai_fukkou/ "東日本大震災 のトピックスを開く")からの復興の象徴として親しまれてきた洋風缶詰「サヴァ缶」は今年5月で製造を終えた。

　震災後の2013年に発売され、オリーブオイル漬けやレモンバジルなど5種類の味付けと、黄や緑のカラフルなパッケージで話題を呼んだ。当初の価格は一般的なサバ缶の2～3倍の360円（税抜き）だったが、計1200万個を売り上げた。

　だが、近年の不漁が直撃した。[岩手県](http://www.asahi.com/area/iwate/ "岩手県 のトピックスを開く")[釜石市](//www.asahi.com/topics/word/釜石市.html "釜石市 のトピックスを開く")の工場が一時休止せざるを得なくなり、販売を担ってきた[第三セクター](//www.asahi.com/topics/word/第三セクター.html "第三セクター のトピックスを開く")の岩手県産（同県[矢巾町](//www.asahi.com/topics/word/矢巾町.html "矢巾町 のトピックスを開く")）の担当者は「原料さえ手に入れば、売り続けたかったのですが」と悔しさをにじませる。

![写真・図版]()

## 漁獲量が低迷　卸売価格は3割高

　サバ缶は手頃な値段に加え、ドコサヘキサエン酸（DHA）などの[栄養素](//www.asahi.com/topics/word/栄養素.html "栄養素 のトピックスを開く")が豊富に含まれる健康食として注目を集めた。10年ほど前からブームとなり、一時は生産が追いつかず、大きく水をあけられていたツナ缶の生産量を逆転した。

　しかし、日本缶詰びん詰レトルト食品協会によると、24年のサバ缶生産量は前年比7%減の2万1千トン。5年前からほぼ半減し、再びツナ缶に抜かれた。協会は「ブームは落ち着いたもののサバ缶の需要はあり、原料の供給不足が響いている」と分析する。

[水産庁](//www.asahi.com/topics/word/水産庁.html "水産庁 のトピックスを開く")によると、23年度（23年7月～24年6月）の全国のサバの漁獲量は約27万1千トン。5年でほぼ半減し、海流の変化や海水温の上昇、乱獲が要因との見方もある。

　各地の漁場環境に影響を与えてきた「黒潮大蛇行」がこの春に7年9カ月ぶりに終息したが、水産庁の担当者は「漁獲量に与える影響は分からない」としている。

![写真・図版]()

　不漁の影響で、卸売価格は上昇傾向で、24年の[東京都](http://www.asahi.com/area/tokyo/ "東京都 のトピックスを開く")[中央卸売市場](//www.asahi.com/topics/word/中央卸売市場.html "中央卸売市場 のトピックスを開く")のサバ1キロあたりの平均卸売価格は560円と、5年前から約3割高くなった。

　資源量の回復をめざし、水産庁は25年度のマサバとゴマサバの漁獲可能量を前年度より約4割少ない約35万トンに設定した。

## サケもサンマも苦境　水産缶詰ピーク時の84%減　72年ぶりの低水準

This Asahi Shimbun article (labeled as a "paid article") reports that the mackerel canned food (saba-kan) boom in Japan has dramatically cooled, with production halving in five years and being overtaken again by canned tuna. The primary cause is a serious shortage of mackerel due to declining catches.

Key facts:
- Mackerel canned production fell to 21,000 tons in 2024, a 7% year-on-year decrease and roughly half of what it was five years ago.
- National mackerel catch in fiscal 2023 (July 2023-June 2024) was about 271,000 tons, roughly halved over five years. Causes cited include changes in ocean currents, rising sea temperatures, and overfishing.
- The wholesale price of mackerel at Tokyo's Central Wholesale Market rose to 560 yen per kilogram in 2024, about 30% higher than five years earlier.
- The Fisheries Agency set the 2025 total allowable catch (TAC) for chub mackerel and spotted mackerel at approximately 350,000 tons, about 40% less than the previous year.
- The "Sava-kan" Western-style canned mackerel, launched in 2013 as a symbol of recovery from the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, ceased production in May (year not stated, presumably 2026). It sold 12 million cans total at 360 yen (excluding tax), initially priced 2-3 times higher than standard mackerel cans.
- A factory in Kamaishi, Iwate Prefecture using Kinka mackerel from Ishinomaki Port had to temporarily suspend operations due to lack of raw materials; purchasing prices for canned mackerel doubled over three years.
- The "Kuroshio meander" (large meander of the Kuroshio Current), which has affected fishing grounds for years, ended in spring 2026 for the first time in 7 years and 9 months, though the Fisheries Agency said the impact on catches is unknown.
- The article mentions that canned seafood overall has declined, and salmon and saury are also facing difficulties, with canned seafood production at 84% below its peak and at a 72-year low.

# ｢あれっサバの価格が上がってない？｣庶民の魚だったサバの高騰が止まらない理由

![](https://tk.ismcdn.jp/mwimgs/0/0/30m/img_00854a117e908ecbee5d371382b9791a27636.jpg)

INDEX

![](https://tk.ismcdn.jp/mwimgs/3/6/570m/img_36bb4de2a34d259d7e4b73291d9b71ac455750.jpg)

「あれっサバの価格上がっていない？」「同じ価格でも切り身が小さくなっていない？」――。食卓、お弁当、外食などでおなじみの脂がのったノルウェーサバ。そのサバの価格が上がり続けています。

かつて2枚1パックで200～300円ほどだったサバのフィーレが400円、500円そして600円と上がっています。今年の買い付けシーズン（8～9月）での現地価格が高騰しているので、少なくとも原料価格の上昇分を転嫁せざるをえず、来年（2026年）はさらに価格が上がる見込みです。フィーレや切り身の大きさを小さくして価格を抑えようとしても、原料価格の上昇に追いつきません。

筆者は1990年からノルウェーサバの買い付けに関わって現地を回っていました。当時は日本のサバのほうが、ノルウェーサバより価値が高かったのですが、今ではその位置づけがすっかり逆転しました。ノルウェーは大きくて脂がのった時期にしかサバを漁獲しないことでブランド化し世界で人気が高まっています。

## 高騰するノルウェーサバ

ノルウェーサバの輸入価格推移を見ると、大きく上昇していることがわかります（2025年は現在の買い付け価格をベース）。2010～2020年頃はキロ200円程度だった原料価格は、その後上昇をはじめ、今年は一気にその3倍程度に高騰してきています。

![](https://tk.ismcdn.jp/mwimgs/7/c/500m/img_7c20622fbc35019f10ff92bdd0610ff3118477.jpg)

なぜこれほどまでに高騰しているのでしょうか？ 主な要因は、2024年に漁獲枠が2割削減されたことです。枠の減少はそのまま供給量の減少を意味します。世界的に需要が高いノルウェーサバは、わずかな供給減でも市場価格が大きく動く構造にあります。たった2割の漁獲枠削減で急上昇するのは、日本的な感覚では少し難しいかもしれません。

日本のサバ（マサバとゴマサバ）の場合は、2023年7月～2024年6月のサバ枠（太平洋系群）を例に取ると、51万トンもの漁獲可能量（TAC）に対して、漁獲量はわずか11万トンと枠を2割しか消化していません。枠と漁獲量が乖離しているので、これでは枠が2割減っても3割減ってもまるでインパクトがないからです。

ところがノルウェーサバの場合は大きく異なります。2割削減となると、漁獲量が実際に2割減少します。日本と異なり、実際に漁獲できる数量よりも、資源の持続性を考えて、漁獲枠が大きく抑えられているからです。このため漁獲枠削減のニュースは、確実に供給量が減るため世界市場が反応して、魚価や買い付け価格に直結するのです。

args.summary:
This is a Japanese article from Toyo Keizai Online (東洋経済オンライン) discussing the dramatic price increase of Norwegian mackerel (サバ), which was traditionally considered a "commoner's fish" (庶民の魚) in Japan. The article is written by a special professor at Tokyo University of Marine Science and Technology who has been involved in Norwegian mackerel purchasing since 1990.

Key points:
- Mackerel fillets that once cost 200-300 yen per 2-piece pack have risen to 400, 500, and now 600 yen. Further increases are expected in 2026 due to rising raw material costs from the current buying season (August-September).
- Norwegian mackerel import prices were around 200 yen per kilogram from 2010-2020, but have now tripled to approximately 600 yen per kilogram.
- The primary cause of the price surge is a 20% reduction in the Norwegian mackerel fishing quota in 2024. Unlike Japan, where quotas don't reflect actual catch (Japan's TAC for the Pacific mackerel stock was 510,000 tons but only 110,000 tons were actually caught, just 20% utilization), Norway sets quotas conservatively for resource sustainability, so quota cuts directly translate to reduced supply.
- Norway has successfully branded its mackerel by fishing only when the fish are large and fatty, gaining worldwide popularity. The author notes that historically Japanese mackerel was valued higher than Norwegian mackerel, but that ranking has now completely reversed.
- Manufacturers are trying to reduce fillet sizes to control prices, but this cannot keep up with rising raw material costs.

**Key points covered:**

1. **Mackerel can price increase (Maruha Nichiro):** Maruha Nichiro announced a price increase of approximately 20 yen on 32 canned mackerel products (boiled mackerel, miso-mackerel, etc.) effective from the 1st of next month (March 2019). This follows a ~10% price increase in September of the previous year. Canned mackerel remains popular due to growing health consciousness. Prices have risen because domestic mackerel demand is growing alongside expanding exports, causing transaction prices to surge.

2. **MSC certification suspension for Atlantic mackerel fisheries:** The Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) - an international nonprofit organization that certifies sustainable fisheries - temporarily suspended its certification for a mackerel fishery spanning 8 countries including Norway, due to overfishing concerns. This could lead to restrictions on mackerel catch. Approximately 85% of Japan's imported mackerel comes from Norway, raising concerns about future shortages. Some supermarkets worldwide may refuse to sell mackerel without the MSC ecolabel.

3. **Other food price increases (Meiji):** Meiji (major food manufacturer) announced price increases on 111 items including Meiji delicious milk and Bulgaria yogurt, effective from April 1 shipments. Milk prices to rise 1.5-3.5%, yogurt 2.3-4.7%. A 400g product could increase by about 10 yen. Reasons include rising logistics and labor costs, plus a hike in raw milk purchase prices for domestic dairy farmers starting April 1.

4. **Public reactions:** Street interviews show mixed reactions - some say a 20 yen increase is tolerable, others say they'd stock up if prices rose to 100 yen. Consumers noted canned foods are useful for disaster preparedness. One person mentioned the coming October consumption tax increase as an additional concern.

イラン情勢が招く『2026年サバ缶・ツナ缶クライシス』をやさしく解説、食卓から缶詰が消えていく本当の理由｜プラスチックパレット株式会社

やさしく解説｜暮らしの値上げ

# イラン情勢が招く『2026年サバ缶・ツナ缶クライシス』をやさしく解説、食卓から缶詰が消えていく本当の理由

初版公開： 最終更新： カテゴリ：**やさしく解説**

**2026年、サバ缶・ツナ缶が値上がりしている理由は3つ重なっています。**①紅海回避で船便は**喜望峰迂回・片道10〜15日長期化**、②ノルウェー産サバ漁獲枠は**前漁期比22％減**で買付価格は**キロ650円超の過去最高**、③タイ漁船は最大**7割が出漁停止懸念**・ベトナム漁業燃料は**2〜2.5倍**。マルハニチロ・はごろもフーズ・ニッスイ・極洋など主要メーカーの値上げが連鎖しています。

3行で覚えておきたいこと

* **船が大回り**している（紅海を避けて、アフリカの南をぐるっと回るので、片道10〜15日も遅れる）。
* **サバが取り合い**になっている（ノルウェー産サバの漁獲枠が2026年は前年比22％減、買付値段は過去最高）。
* **東南アジアの漁船が港から出られない**（中東の原油高で燃料が買えず、タイの漁船は最大7割が止まる見通し）。

## 🤔そもそも、なぜ「中東の話」が「サバ缶の値段」になるんですか？

ピンとこない方が多いと思います。「中東で何かあると原油が上がる」というところまでは何となく知っていても、その先に「サバ缶」が出てくると突然遠く感じる。でも順番に並べてみると、意外と短いつながりなんです。

中東でケンカが起きると、サバ缶が高くなるの？

そうなんです。理由は3つ重なっていて、①船の燃料代が上がる、②船の通り道（紅海）が危なくなって遠回りになる、③東南アジアの漁師さんが「燃料が高くて漁に出られない」と漁を休む──この3つが、すべてサバ缶・ツナ缶のサプライチェーン（原料が日本に届くまでの道のり）にひびくんです。

たとえば、あなたが朝ごはんで食べているノルウェー産サバの塩焼き缶。あのサバはノルウェーの海で獲れて、現地で冷凍されて、コンテナ船に積まれて、地中海・スエズ運河・紅海・インド洋・東南アジア沖を通って日本まで来ます。これが本来の最短ルート。ところがこの「紅海」のあたりで、イエメンのフーシ派という武装勢力が船にミサイルを撃ったり、ドローンで攻撃したりするようになりました。

船会社（マースク、MSC、CMA CGMといった世界の大手）は、危ない海を避けるために、わざわざアフリカの南端「喜望峰」をぐるっと回るルートに切り替えています。地図で見ると一目瞭然で、日本まで来る距離が3,500海里くらい長くなって、片道で10日、往復で約4週間も時間が延びてしまうのです。

ちょっと寄り道：紅海ってどこ？

紅海は、サウジアラビアとアフリカ大陸（エジプト・スーダン）の間にある細長い海です。北の端にスエズ運河があり、地中海とつながっていて、ヨーロッパとアジアを最短で結ぶ「世界の物流のいちばん大事な抜け道」のひとつ。ここが通れなくなると、世界中の船が大回りせざるを得なくなるという、それくらい大切な海なんです。

この章で押さえたいポイント

船が紅海を避けて喜望峰を大回りすると、片道10〜15日も延びる。コンテナの空きも不足する。これが缶詰原料の「届くまでの時間」を延ばす最初の原因。

## 🐟じゃあ、ノルウェーサバって何でそんなに大事なの？

日本のサバ缶は、国産サバとノルウェー産サバの両方を使っています。スーパーの量販店でサバ売り場の半分はノルウェー産（2025年ノルウェー水産物審議会調べ）。脂のりが良くて、サイズも揃っていて、缶詰や塩焼きにぴったりだからです。

ところが2026年、このノルウェー産サバが「とんでもないこと」になっています。漁獲枠（その年に獲っていい量の上限）が、前漁期比で22％も減って16万5,298トンに縮小されました。理由は単純で、大西洋のサバの数が減ってきて、ノルウェー政府が「これ以上獲り続けると魚がいなくなる」と判断したから。資源管理は正しい判断ですが、その分、世界中で「サバの取り合い」が起きています。

みなと新聞によると、2026年期のノルウェー産サバの現地買付値段は、過去最高の1キロ650〜640円（運賃込み価格）に。日本の輸入実績は毎年5万トンほどでしたが、今期は3万トンに届かない可能性もあると報じられています。商社の人たちは「もう大衆魚じゃない、サバは高級魚になった」「『サバクライシス』だ」と話しているそうです（より詳しい数値・出典は[専門版記事](https://plastic-pallet.co.jp/canned-fish-supply-crisis-20260625/)でご確認いただけます）。

ちょっと寄り道：「韓国に買い負け」って何？

ノルウェー産サバを日本に輸入するときの関税は7％。一方、韓国はノルウェー産サバの輸入関税をゼロにしています。同じ品物を買うのに、日本だけ7％余計に払わなければいけない。値段競争で日本が韓国に負けて、日本に来るはずだったサバが韓国に流れていく──これを業界では「買い負け」と呼びます。日本の食卓を支えてきた仕組みが、関税の差で揺らいでいる、そんな現実があります。

この章で押さえたいポイント

ノルウェー産サバは漁獲枠が前漁期比22％減で世界中が取り合い。日本は関税7％を払って買うため、関税ゼロの韓国に「買い負け」する構造リスクを抱えている。

## 🥫ツナ缶も値上がりしているけど、こちらは何が起きているの？

ツナ缶（シーチキン的なやつ）は、世界一の生産国がタイ。日本のスーパーに並ぶツナ缶の多くも、タイで作られたものか、タイから原料を入れて日本で加工したものです。タイにはツナ缶工場が集まっていて、世界中のカツオ・キハダマグロが集まる場所。日本もここから大量に買い付けています。

ちょっと寄り道：ツナ缶の中身、実は3種類あります

スーパーで売られているツナ缶は、原料の魚によって主に3種類に分かれます。**ライトツナ**（カツオが原料・最も安価、いなば「ライトツナ」やはごろも「シーチキンマイルド」など）、**キハダマグロ系**（中価格帯）、**ホワイトツナ**（ビンナガマグロが原料・高級・はごろも「シーチキンファンシー」など）。世界のツナ缶生産量の約68％がカツオ、24％がキハダマグロ。値段が違うのはこの原料魚の違いです。価格高騰局面ではライトツナ（カツオ）の値上げが最も話題になります。

ところが、このツナ缶工場に「原料のカツオ」が届かなくなっています。理由はサバとは少し違って、「漁船が燃料高で出られない」ことが大きい。日本経済新聞（Nikkei Asia）の2026年4月の記事では、タイの水産大県サムットサコーンの商工会議所会頭が「今は新型コロナの時よりも打撃を受けている。コロナの時は漁に行けたが、今は燃料が高すぎて漁に出られない」と話している、と報じられています。

たとえばこんな話

近所のパン屋さんが「小麦粉が3倍に値上がりしたから、明日からお店を開けない」と言ったらどう思いますか？「えっ、じゃあパンが買えない！」となりますよね。タイの漁師さんも今、同じ状況です。「燃料が3倍になったから、漁に出ても赤字。船を港に停めておくしかない」。タイ漁業協会は、4月中旬以降は漁船の最大7割が止まる見通しと予測しています。

この章で押さえたいポイント

ツナ缶世界一の生産国タイで、漁船が燃料高で港から出られない。原料カツオが工場に届かなければ、ツナ缶の供給そのものが細る。

## ⛵東南アジアの漁師さんの話、もう少し詳しく

タイだけじゃなく、ベトナム、インドネシア、フィリピンの漁師さんも同じ状況です。これらの国は、缶詰原料となるカツオ・マグロ・サバ・イワシをたくさん獲ってきた、いわば「世界の海の食料庫」。インドネシアは世界一のカツオ・マグロ漁獲国（年間76.1万トン、FAO 2022年）、フィリピンも年間14.7万トンと上位です。

ベトナム政府系メディア（vietnam.vn）が2026年4月に報じた話では、ベトナム南部・カマウ省（メコンデルタの水産大省）で、漁業用のディーゼル燃料が旧正月前と比べて2〜2.5倍に上昇。同省にある5,165隻の漁船のうち、3月25日時点で274隻が漁の回数を減らし、84隻が完全に操業を停止しているといいます。

なぜ東南アジアの漁師さんがそんなに燃料に苦しんでいるの？

この地域は、ホルムズ海峡（中東のペルシャ湾の入り口）を通る原油への依存度がすごく高いんです。フィリピン・ベトナム・ミャンマーは石油の80％以上をホルムズ経由から調達していて、在庫は約1カ月分しかありません。中東で何かあるとすぐに燃料代が跳ね上がる、いわば「家計の貯金が薄い家」の状態。タイ政府は「漁業者にはB20という安い燃料を優先的に渡す」という対策を作りましたが、それでも採算ぎりぎりです。

ちょっと寄り道：「B20燃料」って？

タイでは、軽油（ディーゼル燃料）にパーム油などのバイオ燃料を20％混ぜた「B20」という安めの燃料があります。通常のディーゼルより1リットルあたり5〜6バーツ（25〜30円）安い。タイ政府は2026年3月、漁船にこのB20を優先的に回す決定をしました。漁業を国の食料安全保障の生命線として守ろうとしている、ということです。

この章で押さえたいポイント

ベトナム・インドネシア・フィリピンの漁船もホルムズ海峡経由の原油に依存。中東情勢が東南アジアの漁業全体を揺さぶり、世界最大カツオ漁獲国インドネシアの供給も影が射す。

## 🍱で、結局、日本の食卓ではいつごろから「サバ缶・ツナ缶クライシス」を感じるの？

実はもう感じ始めています。2024年の日本の水産缶詰生産量は前年比6％減の7万3,742トンで、72年ぶりの低水準を記録しました（日本缶詰びん詰レトルト食品協会調べ）。1952年以来の低水準ということです。総務省の小売物価統計でも、サバの小売価格は2025年3月→2026年3月で約10％上昇しています（東洋経済オンラインより）。

| ニッスイ | 家庭用常温食品47品 | +3〜15%／2025年3月 |
| 極洋 | サバ缶詰など45品 | +5〜30%／2026年4月 |
| いなば食品 | ライトツナ全製品 | 平均+10%／2024年7月 |

家計目線で見ると

サバ缶（160g）は5年前なら100円台で買えました。今は300円前後が珍しくない。福井県小浜市の老舗「福井缶詰」では、年間約79万缶のサバ缶を作るために5社からサバを仕入れていましたが、仕入れ値が前年比で約2倍に上昇。仕入れ先を2社に絞って大量購入でなんとか価格を抑える努力をしたものの、結局値上げを決めた──福井新聞ONLINE（2025年9月）で紹介された事例です。地方の老舗加工屋さんも、本当に苦しい状況です。

### 学校給食・保育園の献立にも影響

家計だけでなく、学校給食や保育園の献立にも影響が出始めています。ツナサンド・サバの味噌煮・シーチキンサラダといった、子どもたちが大好きな定番メニューは、缶詰原料を使うものが多い。日テレNEWS NNNが2026年4月に報じた東京都内の鮮魚店「魚辰」の事例では、近隣の保育園の給食用に長年ノルウェー産サバを卸してきましたが、輸入価格が2025年の1キロ437円から2026年2月には765円（約+75％）に急上昇。「子どもたちが喜んで食べてくれる」と分かっているだけに、原料切り替えや献立変更は心苦しい現実です。自治体の給食予算は年度初めに決まっているため、年度途中で原料価格が急騰すると、献立から特定の魚種が外れていくケースも出てきます。

## 💡私たちはどうすればいいの？暮らしの工夫5つ

ここまで読んで、ちょっと暗い気持ちになった方もいるかもしれません。でも、慌てる必要はありません。日本の食卓には選択肢がたくさんあります。ここからは、家計を守りながら美味しく食べる工夫を5つお伝えします。

### 「特売の日にまとめ買い、食べたら買い足す」を習慣に

缶詰は賞味期限が長い（一般的に2〜3年）ので、特売日に2〜3缶買い置きしておけば、価格が上がる局面でも家計の負担を平らにできます。ただし買いすぎて押し入れの奥で賞味期限を迎えてしまわないように、「ローリングストック」（普段から少しずつ食べて、食べた分を買い足す備蓄方法）を意識すると、防災用備蓄にもなって一石二鳥です。

### サバ・ツナにこだわらず、代替魚をローテーション

EPA・DHAなど青魚の栄養を取りたい方は、サバ缶の代わりにイワシ缶（ペルー産・北海道産）やニシン缶がおすすめ。なお、サンマも近年深刻な不漁が続いていて缶詰生産量も低水準のため、安価な代替としては当てにしにくい状況です。タンパク質補給だけが目的なら、鶏ささみ缶、焼き鳥缶、サラダチキン、大豆缶など選択肢は広いです。みなと新聞によれば、ノルウェー水産物審議会が「高騰のサバ代替、各社ニシン注力」をテーマにセミナーを開催した、と報じられています。

### PB（プライベートブランド）も実は同じ工場で作っていることが多い

スーパーのPB（プライベートブランド）の缶詰は、大手メーカーの工場で作られていることが多く、中身はほぼ同じで価格だけ安いケースが珍しくありません。サバ缶・ツナ缶のPBは特に賢い選択。原料が同じであれば、ブランド品との品質差はそれほど大きくないことが多いです。

### 缶詰だけじゃなく、レトルトパウチもチェック

レトルトパウチ（袋詰めの保存食）は、缶の金属代がかからない分、値上げ幅がやや小さい品目もあります。ゴミも少なく、温める時の調理時間も短い。賞味期限は缶詰よりは短めですが、それでも1〜2年は持つ商品が多いです。

### 旬の生魚・冷凍魚も組み合わせて

缶詰だけでなく、旬の生魚や冷凍魚を上手に組み合わせるのも家計の味方。鮮魚売り場で「特売」「規格外」「お買い得」の札がついた魚は、味は変わらないのにお手頃。土曜の夕方や閉店間際は値引きシールが貼られていることも多いので、そういう時間を狙うのも一つの手です。

## ❓よくある質問

サバ缶やツナ缶って、これからどんどん高くなるんですか？

残念ながら、2026年中はしばらく高い状態が続きそうです。ノルウェー産サバの漁獲枠が前漁期比22％減と大きく減らされたこと、紅海回避で船便が片道2週間遅れること、東南アジアの漁船が燃料高で港から出られないこと、この3つの問題が同時に起きていて、短期解消は難しい状況です。ただし、原油価格や中東情勢が落ち着けば需給が緩和する可能性もあります。普段からローリングストック（食べたら買い足す備蓄方法）を続けて、特売の時にまとめ買いすると、価格変動に対する家計の負担を平らに保てます。

サバ缶の代わりに、何の缶詰なら今までと同じ値段で買えますか？

完全な代替はありませんが、相対的に値上げ幅が小さい品目はあります。ニシン缶、ペルー産イワシ缶、コーン缶、トマト缶などです。タンパク質を補いたい場合は、鶏ささみ缶・焼き鳥缶・大豆缶・サラダチキンも選択肢。お弁当や朝食に使うなら、レトルトパウチの方が缶詰よりゴミが少なく、値上げ幅もやや控えめです。栄養面では青魚（EPA・DHA）を意識するならイワシ缶への切り替えが現実的です。

紅海って遠い話に聞こえます。本当に日本の食卓に関係あるんですか？

とても関係があります。ノルウェーで獲れたサバが冷凍コンテナで日本に運ばれる時、本来はスエズ運河を通って最短ルートで届きます。でも今は紅海で船が攻撃されるリスクがあり、ほとんどの大手船会社（マースク・MSC・CMA CGMなど）がアフリカ南端の喜望峰を大きく回るルートに変更しています。これで欧州〜アジア間の輸送が片道で10〜15日も長くなり、運賃も上がっています。結果として、ノルウェー産サバを使ったサバ缶の値段に直接ひびいています。

ツナ缶はタイの工場で作っているらしいけど、タイで何か起きているんですか？

タイは世界一のツナ缶生産国で、日本のスーパーに並ぶツナ缶の多くもタイで作られています。今そのタイで深刻なのが「漁船が出られない」問題です。中東情勢で原油が高くなり、タイの漁船向け燃料も急騰。タイ漁業協会の予測では商業漁船6,000隻と小規模漁船1.5〜1.6万隻のうち、4月中旬以降は7割が出漁停止見通しとされました。漁船が止まれば原料のカツオが届かず、工場で作れるツナ缶の数も減ります。

缶詰メーカーは値上げばかりしているけど、何か対策はないんですか？

各社それぞれ対策に動いています。マルハニチロは2025年2月から缶詰69品を1〜15％値上げ、はごろもフーズは2026年6月から19品を7.3〜29.4％、ニッスイは2025年3月と2026年3月の二段階で値上げ、極洋は2026年4月から缶詰45品を5〜30％値上げ。同時に仕入れ先の分散、ニシンやペルーイワシなど代替魚の活用、サバ完全養殖の研究、レトルトパウチへのシフトといった取り組みも進めています。ただ原料の根本的な不足は短期間では解消しにくく、値上げが先行している状況です。

This article from Plastic Pallet Corporation explains the 2026 sardine can and tuna can crisis in Japan, driven by three converging factors: (1) ships avoiding the Red Sea and rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope (adding 10-15 days one-way and ~3,500 nautical miles, roughly 4 weeks round-trip), (2) Norway's mackerel catch quota reduced by 22% to 165,298 tons with purchase prices at a record high of 650-640 yen/kg, and (3) Southeast Asian fishing fleets unable to sail due to fuel costs—Thailand's fishing association predicts up to 70% of commercial fishing boats may halt operations from mid-April, while Vietnam's Ca Mau province saw diesel prices rise 2-2.5x.

Key details: Thailand is the world's largest tuna can producer, and tuna cans come in three types (light tuna from skipjack ~68% of world production, yellowfin ~24%, and white tuna from albacore). Southeast Asian nations (Philippines, Vietnam, Myanmar) depend on the Strait of Hormuz for over 80% of their oil with only ~1 month of reserves. Indonesia is the world's largest skipjack/tuna fishing nation (761,000 tons annually per FAO 2022). Japan's mackerel imports from Norway have been cut from ~50,000 to under 30,000 tons, partly because Japan pays 7% import tariffs while South Korea pays 0%, causing Japan to "lose the bidding war."

Impact on Japan: 2024 canned fish production fell 6% year-on-year to 73,742 tons (lowest in 72 years). Mackerel retail prices rose ~10% from March 2025 to March 2026. Sardine cans went from ~100 yen to ~300 yen over five years. Major manufacturers announced price increases: Maruha Nichiro (69 items +1-15%, Feb 2025), Hagoromo Foods (19 items +7.3-29.4%, June 2026), Nissui (47 items +3-15%, March 2025), Kyokuyo (45 items +5-30%, April 2026), and Inaba Foods (light tuna avg +10%, July 2024). School lunches and daycare menus are being affected, with one Tokyo fish shop seeing Norwegian mackerel import prices rise 75% from 437 to 765 yen/kg between 2025 and February 2026.

The article recommends five consumer coping strategies: (1) buy in bulk during sales using "rolling stock" (eat then replenish), (2) rotate alternative fish (herring, Peruvian sardines—not saury due to poor catches), (3) prefer private-label/store-brand cans which are often made in the same factories as brands, (4) consider retort pouches (smaller price increases, less waste), and (5) combine fresh/frozen seasonal fish purchases, taking advantage of discount stickers near closing time.

The article cites numerous sources including JETRO, Reuters/Newsweek Japan, Minato Shimbun, Nikkei, Toyo Keizai, Fukui Shimbun, Nippon TV, Vietnam.vn, and company press releases from Nissui and Kyokuyo. It links to a longer professional version of the article as well as related pieces on naphtha shortages and Middle East infrastructure damage.

# Establecen el límite de captura complementario del recurso caballa al aprobado mediante Resolución Ministerial N° 0449-2023-PRODUCE

# Establecen el límite de captura complementario del recurso caballa al aprobado mediante Resolución Ministerial N° 0449-2023-PRODUCE

## RESOLUCIÓN MINISTERIAL

## Nº 000092-2024-PRODUCE

Lima, 1 de abril de 2024

VISTOS: El Oficio N° 0269-2024-IMARPE/PCD del Instituto del Mar del Perú - IMARPE; el Informe N° 00000130-2024-PRODUCE/DGPARPA de la Dirección General de Políticas y Análisis Regulatorio en Pesca y Acuicultura con el que hace suyo el Informe Nº 00000108-2024-PRODUCE/DPO de su Dirección de Políticas y Ordenamiento; y el Informe Nº 00000296-2024-PRODUCE/OGAJ de la Oficina General de Asesoría Jurídica; y,

CONSIDERANDO:

Que, el artículo 2 del Decreto Ley N° 25977, Ley General de Pesca establece que los recursos hidrobiológicos contenidos en las aguas jurisdiccionales del Perú son patrimonio de la Nación y que, en consecuencia, corresponde al Estado regular el manejo integral y la explotación racional de dichos recursos, considerando que la actividad pesquera es de interés nacional;

Que, el artículo 5 de la citada Ley reconoce a la actividad pesquera como un quehacer permanente de carácter discontinuo, en razón de la naturaleza aleatoria de los recursos hidrobiológicos;

Que, el artículo 9 de la Ley General de Pesca señala que el Ministerio de la Producción, sobre la base de evidencias científicas disponibles y de factores socioeconómicos determina, según el tipo de pesquerías, los sistemas de ordenamiento pesquero, las cuotas de captura permisible, las temporadas y zonas de pesca, la regulación del esfuerzo pesquero, los métodos de pesca, las tallas mínimas de captura y demás normas que requieran la preservación y explotación racional de los recursos hidrobiológicos, y que los derechos administrativos otorgados se sujetan a las medidas de ordenamiento que mediante dispositivo legal de carácter general dicta el Ministerio;

Que, el artículo 5 del Reglamento de la Ley General de Pesca, aprobado por Decreto Supremo Nº 012-2001-PE, dispone que el ordenamiento pesquero se aprueba mediante reglamentos que tienen como finalidad establecer los principios, las normas y medidas regulatorias aplicables a los recursos hidrobiológicos que deban ser administrados como unidades diferenciadas;

Que, mediante Decreto Supremo Nº 011-2007-PRODUCE se aprueba el Reglamento de Ordenamiento Pesquero de Jurel y Caballa, que tiene entre sus objetivos, promover la explotación racional de dichos recursos, la protección del ecosistema marino y la preservación de la biodiversidad, en concordancia con los principios y normas contenidas en la Ley General de Pesca y disposiciones complementarias y/o conexas;

Que, el citado Reglamento de Ordenamiento Pesquero en su numeral 3.2 dispone que el Instituto del Mar del Perú - IMARPE reforzará sus investigaciones sobre los aspectos biológicos, ecológicos y poblacionales de las especies jurel y caballa en el ámbito del dominio marítimo peruano y su zona adyacente, así como sus pesquerías sobre la base de modelos de producción, analíticos y evaluaciones directas por medios hidroacústicos, con el propósito de recomendar las medidas de ordenamiento y de manejo atendiendo a la evolución de las condiciones poblacionales;

Que, el numeral 2.1 del artículo 2 de la Resolución Ministerial Nº 000449-2023-PRODUCE, establece, entre otros, el límite de captura del recurso caballa (Scomber japonicus peruanus) para el periodo anual 2024, en veinte mil doscientas quince (20 215) toneladas, aplicable a las actividades extractivas efectuadas a través de embarcaciones pesqueras de mayor escala;

Que, con Resolución Ministerial N° 00020-2024-PRODUCE se dan por concluidas las actividades extractivas del recurso caballa, efectuadas por embarcaciones pesqueras de mayor escala;

Que, el IMARPE, mediante Oficio N° 0269-2024-IMARPE/PCD remite el documento “OPINIÓN SOBRE PERSPECTIVAS DE EXPLOTACIÓN DEL RECURSO CABALLA PARA EL PERIODO ANUAL 2024” en el que señala: “(…) En la tabla de decisión para la determinación de la cuota anual de captura de caballa, se recomendó considerar tres escenarios con tasas de explotación de 0.051, 0.076 y 0.100 anual, que corresponden a niveles de referencia precautorios (IMARPE, 2023). En caso que el PRODUCE decida incrementar el límite máximo de captura para el presente año (2024), esta no debería superar las 63 mil toneladas para todo tipo de flota, escenario que se presenta a una mortalidad por pesca equivalente a 2.0 veces el aplicado durante el 2023 (IMARPE, 2023) y se encuentra por debajo del Máximo Rendimiento Sostenible (MRS), la cual no afectaría la sostenibilidad de recurso”;

Que, la Dirección General de Políticas y Análisis Regulatorio en Pesca y Acuicultura con el Informe Nº 00000130-2024-PRODUCE/DGPARPA, hace suyo el Informe N° 00000108-2024-PRODUCE/DPO de su Dirección de Políticas y Ordenamiento, mediante el cual recomienda en función a las recomendaciones del IMARPE y al seguimiento de la actividad extractiva de caballa, establecer una cuota complementaria de caballa de 5 775 toneladas para la ejecución de actividades extractivas efectuadas a través de embarcaciones de mayor escala;

Que, la Oficina General de Asesoría Jurídica, a través del Informe Nº 00000296-2024-PRODUCE/OGAJ, señala que resulta legalmente viable la emisión de la citada Resolución Ministerial, conforme a lo propuesto por la Dirección General de Políticas y Análisis Regulatorio en Pesca y Acuicultura;

Con las visaciones del Despacho Viceministerial de Pesca y Acuicultura, de la Dirección General de Políticas y Análisis Regulatorio en Pesca y Acuicultura, de la Dirección General de Pesca para Consumo Humano Directo e Indirecto, de la Dirección General de Supervisión, Fiscalización y Sanción, y de la Oficina General de Asesoría Jurídica; y,

De conformidad con lo dispuesto en el Decreto Ley N° 25977, Ley General de Pesca, su Reglamento, aprobado por Decreto Supremo N° 012-2001-PE; el Decreto Legislativo N° 1047, que aprueba la Ley de Organización y Funciones del Ministerio de la Producción; el Decreto Supremo N° 011-2007-PRODUCE que aprueba el Reglamento de Ordenamiento Pesquero de Jurel y Caballa; y el Reglamento de Organización y Funciones del Ministerio de la Producción, aprobado por Decreto Supremo N° 002-2017-PRODUCE;

SE RESUELVE:

Artículo 1.- Establecimiento del límite de captura complementario del recurso caballa (Scomber japonicus peruanus) para embarcaciones pesqueras de mayor escala en el periodo anual 2024

1.1 Establecer el límite de captura complementario del recurso caballa (Scomber japonicus peruanus) al aprobado mediante Resolución Ministerial N° 0449-2023-PRODUCE, en cinco mil setecientas setenta y cinco (5 775) toneladas, aplicable a las actividades extractivas efectuadas por embarcaciones de mayor escala, a partir del día siguiente de publicada la presente Resolución Ministerial en el diario oficial El Peruano.

1.2 El límite de captura complementario indicado en el numeral 1.1 precedente, puede modificarse en función a los factores biológicos, pesqueros y/o ambientales que estime el Instituto del Mar del Perú - IMARPE, para lo cual remite al Ministerio de la Producción las recomendaciones correspondientes.

1.3 El Ministerio de la Producción concluye las actividades extractivas del recurso caballa (Scomber japonicus peruanus) cuando se alcance o se estime alcanzar el citado límite de captura complementario, o en su defecto, su ejecución no puede exceder del 31 de diciembre de 2024; o cuando el IMARPE lo recomiende por circunstancias ambientales o biológicas.

Artículo 2.- Seguimiento de la pesquería

El IMARPE, en el marco del seguimiento de los principales indicadores biológicos, poblacionales y pesqueros del recurso caballa (Scomber japonicus peruanus), informa y recomienda al Ministerio de la producción las medidas que resulten necesarias.

Artículo 3.- Difusión y cumplimiento

La Dirección General de Políticas y Análisis Regulatorio en Pesca y Acuicultura, la Dirección General de Pesca para Consumo Humano Directo e Indirecto, la Dirección General de Supervisión, Fiscalización y Sanción del Despacho Viceministerial de Pesca y Acuicultura del Ministerio de la Producción realizan las acciones de difusión que correspondan y velan por el cumplimiento de lo dispuesto en la presente Resolución Ministerial; sin perjuicio de las acciones que correspondan ser efectuadas por la Dirección General de Capitanías y Guardacostas de la Marina de Guerra del Perú del Ministerio de Defensa, en el ámbito de sus competencias.

Artículo 4.- Publicación

Disponer la publicación de la presente Resolución Ministerial en la sede digital del Ministerio de la Producción (www.gob.pe/produce), el mismo día de su publicación en el diario oficial El Peruano.

Regístrese, comuníquese y publíquese.

ANA MARIA CHOQUEHUANCA DE VILLANUEVA

Ministra de la Producción

2275217-1

This webpage is a Peruvian official government publication from the digital newspaper "Diario digital del Perú" (lapatria.pe) dated Sunday, August 23, 2026, featuring a Ministerial Resolution from Peru's Ministry of Production (PRODUCE).

The main content is **Ministerial Resolution Nº 000092-2024-PRODUCE**, dated April 1, 2024, in Lima, Peru, which establishes a complementary catch limit for the Pacific chub mackerel (caballa, Scomber japonicus peruanus) resource for large-scale fishing vessels during the 2024 annual period.

Key details of the resolution:

1. **Complementary catch limit**: 5,775 metric tons added to the previously approved limit of 20,215 metric tons set by Resolution Ministerial N° 0449-2023-PRODUCE, applicable to large-scale fishing vessels starting the day after publication in the official gazette El Peruano.

2. **Scientific basis**: The Peruvian Marine Research Institute (IMARPE) provided scientific opinion recommending that if PRODUCE decided to increase the maximum catch limit for 2024, it should not exceed 63,000 tons for all fleet types, which corresponds to a fishing mortality rate 2.0 times that applied in 2023 and remains below the Maximum Sustainable Yield (MRS).

3. **Regulatory framework**: The resolution is based on the General Fisheries Law (Decreto Ley N° 25977), its Regulation (Decreto Supremo N° 012-2001-PE), and the Fisheries Management Regulation for Jack Mackerel and Chub Mackerel (Decreto Supremo N° 011-2007-PRODUCE).

4. **Key provisions**:
   - Article 1: Establishes the 5,775-ton complementary catch limit, which may be modified based on biological, fishery, or environmental factors as determined by IMARPE. Fishing activities conclude when the limit is reached, by December 31, 2024, or when recommended by IMARPE.
   - Article 2: IMARPE will monitor fishery indicators and recommend necessary measures to PRODUCE.
   - Article 3: Various PRODUCE directorates are responsible for dissemination and compliance, along with the Coast Guard (DICAPI) of the Peruvian Navy.
   - Article 4: Publication on PRODUCE's digital platform (www.gob.pe/produce) on the same day as publication in El Peruano.

5. **Signatory**: Ana María Choquehuanca de Villanueva, Minister of Production, signed the resolution (registration number 2275217-1).

## Caballa (Scomber japonicus) Economic Technical Sheet — Peru

This is a technical fact sheet produced by PRODUCE (Peru's Ministry of Production), Office of Economic Studies, covering the economic performance of the mackerel (caballa) fishery in Peru through October 2025.

### Resource Importance
- Caballa is a high-consumption resource in Peru due to its affordable price and high nutritional value, containing high concentrations of Vitamins A and D, and Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA) that help reduce cholesterol and triglycerides.
- The fishery is exclusively for direct human consumption (D.S. 001-2002-PRODUCE), carried out by artisanal, small-scale, and large-scale fleets.
- Landings are primarily destined for the frozen and canned industry for export, with a smaller share going to wholesale fish markets for fresh consumption.
- The resource accounts for 1.1% of GDP contribution and 1.9% of fishing sector contribution (economic), and 0.8% of fishing landings and 2.8% of direct human consumption landings.

### 2025 Fishing Quotas and Landings
- In 2025, a quota of 30,104 metric tons (TM) was set for large-scale vessels (RM N° 270-2025-PRODUCE) and 48,909 TM for artisanal vessels (R.M. N° 273-2025-PRODUCE), totaling a global quota of 79,013 TM for 2025.
- Between January and October 2025, caballa landings reached 38,000 TM, a 30.6% decline compared to the same period in 2024 (55,000 TM).
- Historical annual landings: 56,000 TM (2019), 99,000 (2020), 99,000 (2021), 91,000 (2022), 81,000 (2023), 57,000 (2024*).

### Fleet and Market Statistics
- 1,300 artisanal fishing vessels (EP) declare mackerel as their primary catch resource (CENPAR, 2012).
- 5,800 artisanal fishermen declare mackerel as their primary catch resource (CENPAR, 2012).
- Caballa represents 15.7% of total hydrobiological resources entering wholesale fish markets.
- Average wholesale market price: 4.1 soles per kilogram.

### Production, Trade, and Consumption (2025 Jan-Oct)
- **National production**: 26,400 TM (annual figures 2017-2025: declining trend from 66.2k in 2017 to 26.4k in Jan-Oct 2025), a -38.6% year-on-year decline.
- **Imports**: 3,000 TM (Jan-Oct 2025), down 10.0% year-on-year. Imported product represents 10% of domestic supply (90% national).
- **Domestic sales**: 29,200 TM (Jan-Oct 2025), down 16.8% year-on-year.
- **Exports**: 10,500 TMB / 15.3 million USD-FOB (Jan-Oct 2025), down 19.8% in value and 32.9% in volume year-on-year.
- Export products: Whole, fillet, loin, pieces, solid, grated.
- Export destinations: Côte d'Ivoire (67%), Spain (8%), Italy (5%), Ghana (4%), others (16%).

### Landing Destinations (Jan-Oct 2025)
- Fresh: 44.8%, Frozen: 34.4%, Canned: 20.7%.

### Seasonality and Forecast
- Mackerel seasonality peaks in January, February, and March, when fishing volumes exceed the annual average.
- Historical monthly landing data (2024): January (13,364 TM), February (28,534 TM), March (3,344 TM), April (10,720 TM), May (24,345 TM), June (2,163 TM), July (9,012 TM), August (17,517 TM), September (27,667 TM), October (1,672 TM) — showing high variability.

### Production and Export Zones (Jan-Oct 2025)
- Main landing/transshipment ports: Callao (32%), Tambo de Mora (26%), Ilo (12%), Matarani (4%), others (26%).
- Main production regions: Lima and Callao (62 processing plants), Ica, Lambayeque, Áncash, Arequipa, Moquegua, Piura, Tumbes, La Libertad, Tacna.
- Export ports: Pisco (30%), Callao (20%), Chimbote (5%), Ático (4%), others (41%).
- Key production/export localities: Callao, Paita, Tacna, Chimbote, Tambo de Mora, Coishco.
